chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ibn Mahboub and Ahmad ibn Muhammad regarding the woman
when she dies a puerpera (with post-childbirth bleeding) and her blood is abundant, she is placed up to the navel in a leather bag or a similar clean one, then she is enshrouded after that.

key_terms.الْأَدَمِ: Leather (specifically referring to a leather bag or container)
key_terms.تُكَفَّنُ: She is enshrouded (wrapped in burial cloths)
key_terms.نُفَسَاءَ: A woman who has just given birth, specifically referring to the period of post-childbirth bleeding

ai.seo_question: How is a woman with post-childbirth bleeding treated for ritual burial if she dies?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Kafi addresses the practical challenge of managing abundant post-partum bleeding (nifas) for a deceased woman, prescribing the use of a clean leather bag (adham) to contain the blood up to the navel before final enshrouding. This method ensures ritual purity (taharah) of the body for burial, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on containing impurities that may not cease until death. The use of leather highlights the traditional availability and durability of materials used in ritual preparations during the early Islamic period.
